record.paper_title: Variation Structures: Results and Open Problems
record.original_question: For an invariant i of isolated hypersurface germs f:(C^{n+2},0)->(C,0) that can be written as f=p∘ϕ with ϕ:(C^{n+2},0)->(C^2,0) an isolated complete intersection singularity and p:(C^2,0)->(C,0) a curve singularity, what category C(i) of supplementary coefficient structures on (C^2,0) or on the local complement of the discriminant germ Δ⊂(C^2,0) should be used so that ϕ determines an element S(ϕ)∈C(i) and i(f) can be computed from p and S(ϕ)? In particular, can one define a generalized Dynkin diagram D(p,S), for an isolated curve singularity p and S∈C(i), such that D(p,S(ϕ)) is the Dynkin diagram of f=p∘ϕ whenever f has an isolated singularity?

evidence.quote: Studying the invariants of isolated hypersurface germs f : (Cn+2 , 0) → (C, 0), it is very useful to consider composed germs f = p ◦ ϕ, where ϕ : (Cn+2 , 0) → (C2 , 0) has a manageable discriminant space (for example: ϕ is an isolated complete intersection singularity, in short ICIS), and p : (C2 , 0) → (C, 0) is a curve singularity.

Problem # 1. Find the category C(i) for other invariants. For example, ﬁnd a category C(i) such that any ICIS ϕ (as above) gives an element S(ϕ) ∈ C(i). Moreover, deﬁne a “generalized Dynkin diagram” D(p, S) for any (isolated) curve singularity p and S ∈ C(i) in such a way that D(p, S(ϕ)) is the Dynkin diagram of f = p ◦ ϕ (provided that f has isolated singularity).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $f:(\mathbb{C}^{n+2},0)\to(\mathbb{C},0)$ be a holomorphic germ defining an isolated hypersurface singularity. Assume $f$ admits a factorization $f = p\circ\varphi$, where:

(a) $\varphi:(\mathbb{C}^{n+2},0)\to(\mathbb{C}^{2},0)$ is an isolated complete intersection singularity (ICIS), with discriminant germ $\Delta\subset(\mathbb{C}^{2},0)$; and

(b) $p:(\mathbb{C}^{2},0)\to(\mathbb{C},0)$ is a reduced plane curve singularity.

Fix an invariant $i$ of isolated hypersurface singularities (such as the Milnor number, the geometric genus, the spectrum, the monodromy representation, the Seifert form, the Hodge or mixed Hodge structure on vanishing cohomology, or the Coxeter–Dynkin diagram).

The problem is to construct a category $\mathcal{C}(i)$ of "supplementary coefficient structures" on the germ $(\mathbb{C}^{2},0)$, or equivalently on the complement of the discriminant $\Delta$ in $(\mathbb{C}^{2},0)$ (for instance: local systems, perverse sheaves, variation structures, or some enriched analogue), satisfying the following two properties.

(1) Every ICIS $\varphi$ as above functorially determines an element $S(\varphi)\in\mathcal{C}(i)$.

(2) For every reduced plane curve singularity $p$ and every object $S\in\mathcal{C}(i)$, one can define a "generalized Dynkin diagram" $D(p,S)$, in a way that depends only on $p$ and $S$, such that whenever $f=p\circ\varphi$ has isolated singularity one has the equality
$$ D(p,S(\varphi)) = \text{(the Coxeter–Dynkin diagram of }f\text{)},$$
and more generally $i(f)$ can be recovered from $p$ and $S(\varphi)$ alone.

For which invariants $i$ (beyond those for which it is already known) does such a category $\mathcal{C}(i)$ and such an assignment $D(p,S)$ exist, and how can it be constructed?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as Problem #1 in a list of open problems on variation structures by A. Némethi. Web searches did not turn up any subsequent work providing a general categorical answer or a general construction of $D(p,S)$ for invariants beyond the cases originally known (e.g. the Seifert/variation structure case). The problem appears to remain open in its general form.

status_evidence.snippet: Problem #1: Find the category C(i) for other invariants ... define a generalized Dynkin diagram D(p,S) ... such that D(p,S(φ)) is the Dynkin diagram of f = p ∘ φ.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is explicitly listed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Coxeter-Dynkin diagrams and singularities (Gabrielov)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of Coxeter–Dynkin diagrams of isolated hypersurface singularities; no general categorical construction D(p,S) for composed singularities is presented.
status_evidence.claim: Standard surveys on Dynkin diagrams for singularities do not record a resolution of the problem.
